speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: These were the words of former Minister for National Development, Mr Mah Bow Tan in a 2010 commentary and were similarly echoed by Mr Bobby Chin, Chairman of the HDB in the HDB’s FY18 annual report.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Fast forward to 2021, as we grapple with the age of disruption, the complexities of the future economy and transitioning to a post-COVID-19 world, it is imperative that we take stock of our housing situation and approach to housing, such that they continue to meet the housing needs and aspirations of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Let us first take stock of the existing housing model in Singapore today, particularly as it relates to rental housing.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: When HDB first started building flats, it built rental flats.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: From 1960 to 1965, there were 42,408 rental flats versus only 2,967 home ownership flats, given the Government’s home ownership scheme really only started in 1964.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: After decades of pushing for home ownership, when HDB resumed the rental building programme in 2007, only 1-room and 2-room flats were built.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: HDB rentals today take on three different forms, the Public Rental Scheme (PRS), Interim Rental Housing (IRH) and Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS).

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The vast majority of flats, however, relate to the Public Rental Scheme.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Flats under the PRS in its current form are supposed to be heavily subsidised to cater to Singaporean households who, in the HDB’s words, have no other housing options.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Another eligibility criterion is the low total household gross income threshold of not exceeding $1,500 per month, with monthly rents for a 1-room flat ranging from $26 a month to $205 a month and a 2-room flat from $44 a month to $275 a month.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Interim Rental Housing is similar to the PRS in that it is for low-income households with no family support and no other housing options, where the HDB will consider offering IRH on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Lastly, the PPHS was part of the enhanced Marriage and Parenthood Package and helps to temporarily house families as they await the completion of their new flats.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Rents are between $400 and $500 for 2-room flats, $600 to $900 for 3-room flats, and $1,500 for 4-room flats, depending on their location.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Fundamentally, I believe that there needs to be a greater diversity of housing options but, more urgently, the key problem, in my view, is that there is a severe shortage of HDB rental flats in its various forms today and supply is simply insufficient to meet current demands.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: As I have noted earlier, there were 63,773 rental flats as of March this year, the vast majority of which would comprise 1-room and 2-room flats under the PRS.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In response to my Parliamentary Question (PQ) in May earlier this year, Minister Desmond Lee noted, and I quote, that: “There are currently about 31,000 1-room and 31,000 2-room flats.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: We have sufficient supply for households who need these flats”.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: However, I understand from another PQ filed by Member Ms Nadia Samdin that the average waiting time for a rental flat has lengthened to about five months.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I understand from a fellow Workers' Party Member of Parliament that HDB shared in a reply in late May that HDB is facing an island-wide shortage of 1-room flats and that all four zones are having an estimated waiting time of about six months from date of registration.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I recognise that part of this is also related to COVID-19-related constraints, such as taking up a longer time to spruce up flats that have been returned to the HDB before they are let out to new tenants.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I am sure Members of this House would have received many requests by your residents to assist them with an appeal for a rental flat from the HDB, just as I have.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: So, while we may say that a wait time of two months pre-COVID-19 is “okay”, the eligibility conditions around public rental flats are highly restrictive.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In fact, the total household income cap of $1,500 a month is even lower than the Average Monthly Household Income from Work of the lowest 10% of resident employed households!

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Just how many truly needy citizen families have we excluded as a result of the tight eligibility conditions?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: A similar situation can be said for the PPHS.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Again, in response to my PQ in May, there were 110 2-room, 570 3-room and 60 4-room flats for the PPHS, or a total of 740 flats.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: As the Minister noted, the supply of PPHS flats is limited and depends on the availability of vacant flats, such as those in vacated blocks not immediately needed for redevelopment.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I acknowledge that in HDB’s press release in August, the number of existing PPHS flats is now 840, with another 800 more flats to be set aside over the next two years.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: It is commendable that HDB is doubling the number of PPHS flats.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In absolute numbers, however, we are dealing with a very low base today, given that the demand for such flats has far exceeded the limited supply.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Other than addressing the current demand and supply imbalance, just simply, why rental housing though?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Here, I would like to share five aspects on why creating a subsidised and expanded public rental scheme for the wider population would be beneficial to Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Going for a BTO flat has been the avenue to provide couples an affordable home for their future families.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: And as I have shared, the odds of securing a PPHS flat is equally low.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Singaporeans who are more financially well to do have access to open market HDB or private residential rentals or even accessing serviced residences and co-living apartments.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The desire by millennials to have a space of their own is well reported, with a Business Times (BT) article dated 18 June highlighting that more Singaporeans are moving out of family homes into formerly expat-dominated co-living properties and serviced residences.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: On 11 September, Today published a similar article, titled “Affluent and craving space to grow, more single millennials leave the nest for greater freedom”.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Should we not cater to the changing housing needs and aspirations of all our millennials today regardless of their income?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Undoubtedly, a good number of couples have been affected by construction delays in existing BTO projects; and with low odds of securing a new BTO project, given high application rates, without a place of their own, are left with no choice but to rethink their family planning decisions.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: We need to recognise that everyone’s circumstances change all the time and we should cater to Singaporeans’ housing needs across life stages, as people may decide it is most appropriate to rent or buy at different stages of their lives.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Besides, by providing young couples with an alternative to save up larger amounts of capital which would have otherwise been locked up in their housing asset, this might encourage them to start families at a younger age and be open to having more children.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The need for a dynamic and flexible workforce today would mean that individuals may need to take greater calculated risks or seek alternative pathways to advance their careers.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: What we have not adequately considered is that individuals require the financial freedom to pursue these tough choices.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Would you still take up that overseas posting or pursue further graduate studies if you are tied to a significant mortgage or if it means your MOP would have to be extended?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Capital is an essential source of economic growth and, more so than before, largely dependent on productivity.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Allowing rental housing to play a bigger role compared to home ownership could free up capital for individuals and, arguably, result in less of a rentier economy in Singapore and encourage more to have an entrepreneurial mindset.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: This brings me to my fourth point on having to adapt well to a major trend today: the rise of the gig economy.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: According to MOM, there has been an increase in freelancers from around 200,000 in 2016 to 228,000 in 2020, a 14% increase over the past four years.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Many of these freelancers do not have a regular source of income, thereby suffering from income insecurity during times of economic crises.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: While it is important for freelancers to exercise financial prudence when calculating what they "can afford", it is not easy to determine with pinpoint accuracy their level of earnings even on a day-to-day basis, much less over the next few years; and signing up for a 25-year mortgage may not be the most prudent decision.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Fifthly, and, critically, we need to promote true inclusivity and get rid of the stigma of HDB rental housing.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In her book "This is What Inequality Looks Like", Assoc Prof Teo You Yenn described the poor design of rental flats and frequent observations of cramped, distinctively damp and pungent smell of poorly ventilated corridors.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The design of new-build rental flats may have improved, but there still remains a stigma associated with HDB public rental flats, which does not necessarily go away even if the Government has integrated such flats within BTO estates or, potentially, in prime location public housing estates.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: This is evident even in a number of replies to my appeals to HDB for a rental flat for my residents, where the HDB officer describes HDB rental flats as being, and I quote “heavily subsidised to meet the housing needs of poor and needy citizen families who are unable to afford home ownership flats, have no other housing options and no family support”.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Renting an HDB flat need not and should not be seen as a sign that you are poor and needy and our position on rentals need to reflect that.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Above all, I think one of the biggest misconceptions is that home ownership is superior to home renting and that money spent on renting is money down the drain.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: To use an analogy from the insurance world: is a whole life insurance policy necessarily superior to that of term insurance?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Certainly, with a whole life policy, there will be a cash value attached to the policy should it be cancelled or sold after a certain period of time.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: This is non-existent for a term life insurance policy.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Yet, a common saying in the insurance industry is, “buy term, invest the rest”, where one separates the protection element in an insurance policy from the investment motive.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I believe the same can be applied to housing and the saying that “tenants pay subsidised rents but own nothing” is only a half-truth.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: It is comforting to know that I am not alone in my views on this.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: On 18 October, BT ran an interesting article, “Renting can be a viable alternative to owning a private home in Singapore”.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: As the title suggests, the author ran a simulation and derived an outcome where, financially, the difference between renting and buying is negligible.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: But the math, however, need not be true only for high-end private residential property.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Singapore today has a high home ownership rate close to 90%, similar to China.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: This is significantly above that of the OECD average of 68%.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Importantly, I highlight that within the OECD countries, Switzerland and Germany have the lowest home ownership rates of 38% and 44% respectively, while, at the same time, having one of the highest GDP per capita and Human Development Index (HDI) scores globally.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The correlation between home ownership and the level of prosperity of a country may not be as clear-cut.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Home ownership is thus more of a preference than a superior option per se.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Quality rental housing need not be an oxymoron and, globally, it is already well demonstrated that rental housing can be affordable, desirable and effective as a means to house a population.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: About half of social housing units are owned directly by the municipal government and the rest by state-subsidised, not-for-profit co-operatives.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Private developers who build affordable housing projects must allow the city to rent half of the new apartments to lower-income residents, while the developer leases out the remaining units.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: As rents are regulated by the city government, affordability and access are maintained, with social integration a natural outcome of such housing arrangements.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: As shared by Mr Kurt Puchinger, former Director of Planning in the City of Vienna, "We don’t want to have a situation where you can identify the social status of a person by their home address".

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: With the appropriate framework of rights and responsibilities in place, both the public and private sectors can work together to achieve our social policy goals.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Given the relative resilience of the residential sub-sector as compared to retail and commercial during the COVID-19 pandemic, I am confident that there will be no lack of interest by private developers to partner HDB in coming up with innovative Build-to-Rent housing solutions if the Government is willing to take this bold step in public-private partnership.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Nominated Member of Parliament Mr Cheng Hsing Yao, in his speech earlier this year, also suggested a Build-to-Rent model for Singapore, calling for the Government to encourage active and responsible participation by the private sector in this regard.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Looking at international case studies in Australia, the Queensland government is partnering the construction industry to deliver affordable rental housing through new Build-to-Rent developments – one of which is being developed by one of the Singapore-listed firms as well.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Even in China, where home ownership is one of the highest in the world, just like Singapore, the government has been encouraging the development of more rental-only projects through policy changes since 2018.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I acknowledge Minister Desmond Lee's comments at the Committee of Supply debates earlier this year that there is a rental market out there for people to rent smaller units, both in the private market, as well as in HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: But the aim here is really to look at the aspirations of Singaporeans and see how we can provide the support for those aspirations through providing rental options from the HDB.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: We do not simply accept that Singaporeans can all purchase private property or resale HDB flats and stop launching new BTO projects, do we?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Rentals of the HDB flats could then be priced at levels in between current HDB public rentals and HDB open market rentals.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: This could also be restricted to Singaporeans, just like our current BTO and rental schemes today.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In addition, if home ownership is still an ideal the Government would like to champion, renters may be able to own their flats, albeit in a different manner.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: As it is, we have observed that the yields and yield spreads of residential REITs listed overseas are among the lowest among real estate sub-sectors, a reflection of the attractiveness of residentials to the financial markets and providers of capital.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Just as how REITs allow for the fractional ownership of commercial property assets, the stock of HDB rental units can similarly be held in a REIT structure, be it a public or private REIT.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: This would also have the additional benefit of supporting the financing of the construction of new rental flats and is self-sustaining, reducing the cash costs on the part of the Government.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: For Singaporeans, rather than take a 90% LTV loan for more than half our working lives, those who wish to can put up an amount of capital we are comfortable with into ownership of this REIT, with redemptions controlled to minimise speculation, just as how there are Minimum Occupation Period (MOP) restrictions for BTO flats today.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Singaporeans can enjoy the benefits of renting, while also truly say that they own a HDB flat, or a part of Singapore's entire stock of HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: To conclude, Mdm Deputy Speaker, the idea of an expanded public rental scheme by HDB is not new.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Let us also remember that the concept of leasing is not new to HDB.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The concept of owning a HDB flat is a misnomer where Singaporeans have signed with HDB a lease agreement and not exactly a sale and purchase agreement, albeit one which is for 99 years, lease payments are paid upfront and you are able to take out a loan to pay for it.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Further, the concept of having shorter leases is also not new.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: It really is simply just a difference in mode of payment, where the lease payment is paid upfront, as compared to regular monthly payments in the case of conventional open market short-term leases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Since Independence, we have strived to support the diverse aspirations of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In recent years, the Government has been engaging citizens, more deeply and extensively, to consult and co-create solutions on issues we all care deeply about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This includes our public housing programme, which is unique and unlike any others in the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Home ownership has been the cornerstone of our public housing policy and a key tenet of Singapore's social compact.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It was an audacious goal – to make it easy for citizens of a young, developing nation, to own their homes, to give families stability, develop a sense of rootedness and a concrete stake in Singapore's progress.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Beyond being homes, HDB flats are also valuable assets that can be monetised to supplement their owners' income during their retirement years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This compares with 65% in the US, 72% in the EU and 63% in Australia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This reflects the priority the Government places on keeping home ownership attainable for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: New flats are priced with a generous subsidy and supplemented with grants for affordability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For many Singaporeans, these housing subsidies constitute one of the most significant bundles of subsidies that they enjoy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have also provided a steady supply of public housing over the years to meet demand and provide affordable and inclusive public housing for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: While our home ownership rate is high, we recognise that some may not be quite ready for home ownership and require some additional assistance and support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: That is why we provide subsidised rental housing options targeted at specific needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For low-income households with no other housing options, we provide highly subsidised rental housing under the Public Rental scheme, as a social safety net.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB has and will continue to exercise flexibility on a case-by-case basis, where necessary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For families who need an interim housing option while waiting for their BTO flats, we rent out flats under the Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme, or PPHS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also provide Interim Rental Housing for lower-income households who need temporary accommodation while waiting to buy or collect the keys to their own flat and have no other housing options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, given the significant subsidies involved, such rental options are very targeted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our aim is to help households in public rental eventually achieve home ownership as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB and social agencies work closely to support rental households in overcoming the various challenges that they face.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, through Community Link, or ComLink, Government agencies and community partners work to support families with young children living in public rental flats, to help them achieve stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: When families are ready, they can also obtain housing grants and personalised guidance from HDB's Home ownership Support Team on budgeting and the flat-buying process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our home ownership policies also support our family formation policies, which reflect another important aspiration of many Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The recent World Values Survey in 2020 showed that families are important to Singaporeans and most want to have children, preferably two.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Changing societal trends may reshape how some Singaporeans perceive home ownership.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: More Singaporeans are remaining single and may wish to own their own homes, too, while some young people who do intend to get married eventually might also desire to live apart from their parents for a few years, as alluded to by Mr Louis Chua.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These are diverse aspirations and, understandably, lead to questions about whether our public housing policy can be more flexible in accommodating them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Single buyers have access to housing grants and can buy smaller BTO units in non-mature estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: While our overall housing policy continues to support families, we recognise the home ownership aspirations that many singles have.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For instance, some singles have had to forgo opportunities of forming families of their own because of caregiver responsibilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Seniors who are single also tend to be more vulnerable than those who can count on the support of their spouses, children and even grandchildren.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In such cases, home ownership can be material in improving a person's well-being as well as financial security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are very mindful of the circumstances of this group and will continue to study ways to assist them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As for expanding the range of subsidised rental offerings, especially for medium- to long-term accommodation, we would need to consider this very carefully.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is common to see young people renting their own apartments in big cities all over the world, but this is largely unsubsidised and subject to market forces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For instance, the city that one works in could be very far from one's hometown and, hence, living with one's parents is out of the question.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In some societies, it is a norm for young adults to move out from their parents' homes, even if they do not work in a different city.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The rent that such tenants pay is a consumption expense, which could have gone into home ownership, if home ownership was within reach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But without public housing subsidies that support home ownership, some end up renting for many years, or even for life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In Singapore, a wide range of open market rental options are also available in HDB and private estates, of varying sizes, locations and rent levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Amongst these offerings, co-living appears to be increasingly popular amongst the younger generation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have observed more Singaporeans taking up such co-living options, compared to previously where it mainly catered to foreigners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will continue to study and monitor this trend further.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Louis Chua suggests that there could still be a gap in the rental offerings today, as there are Singaporeans who prefer to rent instead of own for a certain number of years but are not eligible for public rental and do not wish to take up open market or private sector options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Louis Chua suggested that HDB rent out flats at rates set at a discount to that of the open market to meet demand from these groups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We see the provision of a subsidised rental option as a means towards achieving home ownership because we believe in the benefits that home ownership brings to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Members of this House would be aware that we recently launched the new Prime Location Public Housing model, or PLH for short.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In developing the new model, we embarked on an extensive engagement exercise to seek views from Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As I have shared, we continue to believe in the benefits of homeownership for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Apart from this, without substantial rental subsidies from the Government, most Singaporeans would be unlikely to find it attractive to pay market rent using cash.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Flat owners who purchase a flat of sufficient lease and complete the loan payments are assured of a roof over their heads for the rest of their lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The same considerations would apply, if we were to contemplate the provision of subsidised rental options for public housing in the manner that Mr Louis Chua has described.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, we introduced the 2-room Flexi scheme in 2015 as a new housing option to better cater to the diverse housing needs of families, singles and seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For seniors buying 2-room Flexi flats, they have the option of choosing —

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
